intro: Phoning in English can be scary: you can't see the other person and you can't use gestures. Luckily, phone calls follow very fixed phrases. This lesson gives you the phrases to call, answer, take or leave a message and deal with a bad line.
objectifs: Say who you are and ask to speak to someone (This is…, Can I speak to…?).
Answer the phone and ask the caller to wait (Hold on, I'll put you through).
Leave a clear message on voicemail or with a person, and say a phone number clearly.
Deal with problems: a bad line, asking someone to repeat or spell, a wrong number.

sections.titre: Calling and saying who you are
texte: On the phone, don't say “I am Paul”: say “This is Paul” or “It's Paul” (informal). Use “Paul speaking” when you answer.
To ask for someone: “Can I speak to Ms Ndiaye, please?” (neutral), “Could I speak to…?” (more polite), “Is Paul there?” (informal). Use “speak to” in this phrase, not “talk with”.
Then say why you are calling: “I'm calling about…” (+ noun) or “I'm calling to…” (+ verb).

lignes: Could I speak to Mrs Owusu, please?
I'm calling about the job advert.
I'm calling to confirm my appointment.

exemples: Hi, it's Sophie. Is Marc there?
Good morning. This is Dr Eto's office. I'm calling to change your appointment.

sections.titre: Answering and asking the caller to wait
texte: At work, answer with the company name and your first name: “Good morning, Lumina Bank, Sara speaking. How can I help you?” At home, just “Hello?”.

To find out who is calling: “Who's calling, please?” / “May I ask who's calling?” (formal). To ask the caller to wait: “Hold on, please.”, “Just a moment.”, “One moment, please.” To connect the caller to another person: “I'll put you through.”
If the person is not free: “I'm sorry, she's not available at the moment.”, “He's in a meeting.”, “She's out of the office today.”, “The line is busy.” (US; UK: “The line's engaged.”).
exemples: Who's calling, please? — It's Ama Mensah from Ghana Air.
Hold on, I'll put you through.
I'm sorry, Mr Diallo is in a meeting. Can I take a message?

texte: With a person: “Could you tell her that I called?”, “Could you ask him to call me back?”, “Can I leave a message?”. The person writes it down: “Can I have your name and number?”
On voicemail, follow a short plan: who you are, the time or day, why you are calling, what you want, your number (twice), a word to finish.
To say a number: read the numbers one by one; 0 is “oh” (or “zero”, especially in the US); two of the same number: “double” (UK): 077 = “oh double seven”. Make groups with pauses.

lignes: Hi, this is Lina Haddad from the Liège office.
I'm calling about the meeting on Friday.
Could you call me back before five?
My number is oh four nine five, two two three, eight one six. That's 0495 223 816.

sections.note: With a pronoun, “call back” separates: “call me back”, “I'll call you back”. Don't say “recall”: it means “remember” or “ask people to return a faulty product”.

texte: Don't be afraid to ask someone to repeat: it is normal and polite. “Sorry, could you say that again?”, “Could you speak a bit more slowly, please?”, “Could you speak up, please?” (louder).
For a name or an address: “Could you spell that, please?”. For a bad line: “Sorry, the line is bad.”, “You're breaking up.” (I can only hear parts), “I can't hear you very well.”
For a mistake: “Sorry, I think you've got the wrong number.” To finish: “Thanks for calling.”, “Speak to you soon.”, “Bye!”
exemples: Sorry, you're breaking up. Can I call you back?
Could you spell your surname, please? — Yes, it's O-W-U-S-U.

texte: Phone calls use many phrasal verbs (lesson 72). Learn them as blocks.

lignes: I'll call you back in ten minutes.
I'll put you through to sales.
I couldn't get through to the bank.

exemples: I called three times, but nobody picked up.
She was angry and she hung up.

formule: Hello, this is… · Could I speak to…? · I'm calling about… · Can I leave a message? · Could you ask him to call me back? · My number is…
prononciation: Say numbers in groups of 3 or 4, with a pause and a rising voice except on the last group: “oh four nine five ↗ | two two three ↗ | eight one six ↘”.
“Double” in numbers: 0044 = “oh oh double four” or “double oh double four” (UK).
“I'll” is short: /aɪl/; “I'll call you back” = /aɪl ˈkɔːl ju ˈbæk/. The l in “call” is dark, at the back of the mouth.
Spell with the English alphabet (lesson 19): careful with A /eɪ/, E /iː/, I /aɪ/, G /dʒiː/, J /dʒeɪ/, R /ɑː/, W /ˈdʌbljuː/.
On the phone, speak a little more slowly and say the ends of words clearly: people can't read your lips.
erreurs: Hello, I am Karim.
Hello, this is Karim. / Hello, it's Karim.
On the phone: this is / it's.
Can I talk with Mr Smith?
Can I speak to Mr Smith, please?
Fixed phrase: speak to.
Who is at the phone?
Who's calling, please?
To ask who is calling.
Wait, I pass you Mr Diallo.
Hold on, I'll put you through to Mr Diallo.
Connect a caller = put through.
Can you recall me?
Can you call me back?
Phone again = call back.
She's not there for the moment.
She's not available at the moment.
Say “at the moment”.
I call you back in five minutes.
I'll call you back in five minutes.
A promise made now: will (lesson 49).
You have made a wrong number.
I think you've got the wrong number.
Fixed phrase: wrong number.

dialogue.contexte: Brice, in Yaoundé, phones a company in Toronto about his job application.
lignes: Good morning, Maple Tech, Jenny speaking. How can I help you?
Good morning. This is Brice Nkoulou. Could I speak to Mr Wilson, please?
Saying who you are + asking for someone.
May I ask what it's about?
I'm calling about my job application for the developer position.
Hold on, please… I'm sorry, Mr Wilson is in a meeting. Can I take a message?
Asking him to wait; offering to take a message.
Yes, please. Could you ask him to call me back?
Of course. Could you spell your surname?
N-K-O-U-L-O-U. And my number is plus two three seven, six nine nine, four five, double two, eight one.
Thank you. I'll give him the message.

I left a message on her voicemail.

exercices.consigne: Write the message you leave on a garage's voicemail: your car has a problem and you would like an appointment this week. Follow the six steps in section 3.
items: Model answer

Hi, this is Paul Mbarga. It's Monday morning, about nine o'clock. I'm calling about my car, a grey Toyota. It makes a strange noise when I brake. I'd like an appointment this week, if possible on Wednesday or Thursday. Could you call me back on oh six nine nine, four five two, one one eight? That's 0699 452 118. Thanks a lot. Bye!

a_retenir: Say who you are: This is… / It's… (never “I am…”); when you answer: Sara speaking.
Ask: Could I speak to…, please? — Who's calling? — Hold on, I'll put you through.
Messages: Can I take / leave a message? Could you ask him to call me back? My number is…
Numbers: one by one, 0 = oh, 77 = double seven, in groups.
Problems: Could you say that again / speak up / spell that? You're breaking up. Wrong number.
